problem: Cortés's Second Letter puts his losses at about 150 Spaniards (plus 45 horses) and over 2,000 allies, not 'hundreds of Spaniards'. The higher figures come from Díaz and others.

fix.digest: After Moctezuma's death and weeks of fighting, the Spaniards and their Tlaxcalan allies try to slip out along the causeway at night with as much gold as they can carry. They are discovered, the bridges are cut, and many drown or are killed. Cortés gives his losses as about 150 Spaniards and more than two thousand allies; other witnesses put the Spanish dead far higher, and the real number is unknown.

problem: Cortés's Third Letter gives the siege as seventy-five days (from 30 May to 13 August), not 'some eighty'.

fix.digest: Cortés reports that after seventy-five days of siege, by his count, with most of the city destroyed, a brigantine captured Cuauhtémoc's canoe on the lake and brought him to Cortés. He writes of the hunger and dead in the last quarter held by the defenders in sober-sounding numbers, and as if the outcome had been God's will.
